meta.title: CGIAR Climate Adaptation and Mitigation Taxonomy

facets.name: Climate risk
facets.def: Potential for adverse consequences of climate and its determinants and manifestations; the adaptation-side anchor. Prefix CRK_.

facets.name: Climate driver
facets.def: Causal-side mitigation anchor: greenhouse gases, emission sources, and the Climate change and Climate variability drivers. Prefix CDI_.

facets.name: System
facets.def: Agri-food and ecological systems and components acted upon or affected. Prefix SYS_.

facets.name: Intervention
facets.def: An action or activity taken to adapt or mitigate. Prefix INT_.

facets.name: Output
facets.def: A tangible product, service, or deliverable produced by an intervention. Prefix OUT_.

facets.name: Outcome
facets.def: A neutral state or property that changes as a result; direction applied at tagging time. Prefix OTC_.

facets.name: Impact
facets.def: A long-term or higher-order effect. Prefix IMP_.

facets.name: Adoption pathway
facets.def: A modifier describing the stage or degree of uptake and scaling; never used alone. Prefix ADP_.

facets.name: Breeding trait
facets.def: A heritable characteristic targeted by breeding. Prefix TRT_.

facets.name: Stakeholder
facets.def: An actor or social group involved in or affected by climate action. Prefix STK_.

facets.name: Cross-cutting concept
facets.def: A construct that qualifies other terms rather than occupying a position on the results chain: normative principles, named ways of working, and greenhouse-gas accounting constructs. Prefix CCC_. A term belongs here only if it cannot fill a pathway element on its own; if it can, it belongs in a chain facet.

levels.name: L1
levels.def: Top-level concept in its facet; Parent ID is blank.

levels.name: L2
levels.def: A kind of an L1 term.

levels.name: L3
levels.def: A kind of an L2 term.

levels.name: L4
levels.def: A kind of an L3 term.

levels.name: L5
levels.def: A kind of an L4 term.

levels.name: L6
levels.def: A kind of an L5 term.

pathwayStages.name: Rationale
pathwayStages.def: Establishes why a term counts: climate risks and drivers.

pathwayStages.name: Outcome
pathwayStages.def: The state that changes as a result.

pathwayStages.name: Stakeholder
pathwayStages.def: The actors, sitting alongside the results-chain.

pathwayStages.name: Cross-cutting
pathwayStages.def: Concepts, principles, and traits that apply across the chain.

scopes.name: Adaptation + Mitigation
scopes.def: Serves both; a single row carrying both tags.

adaptationTags.name: Adaptation-conditional
adaptationTags.def: General term; counts as adaptation only in combination. Condition in Adaptation condition.

mitigationTags.name: Mitigation-conditional
mitigationTags.def: Counts as mitigation only in combination. Condition in Mitigation condition.

impactAreas.name: Climate adaptation & mitigation
impactAreas.def: CGIAR Impact Area; used for terms specific to the climate frame.

impactAreas.name: Cross-cutting
impactAreas.def: Not tied to one Impact Area; used for stakeholders, principles, and cross-cutting concepts.

relationTypes.name: addresses
relationTypes.def: An intervention or trait acts to reduce the harm of a climate hazard (the object).

relationTypes.name: applies-to
relationTypes.def: An intervention applies to a system; a cross-cutting concept applies to an intervention, outcome or impact.

relationTypes.name: builds
relationTypes.def: Strengthens a capacity, capability or asset.

relationTypes.name: composed-of
relationTypes.def: Partitive relation: the subject is composed of the object.

relationTypes.name: emits
relationTypes.def: Mitigation: the subject (a system) emits the object (a greenhouse gas). Identifies a source; does not by itself make a term count as mitigation.

relationTypes.name: measured-by
relationTypes.def: An outcome is measured by an index or measure.

relationTypes.name: part-of
relationTypes.def: Partitive relation: the subject is part of the object.

relationTypes.name: produces
relationTypes.def: An intervention produces an output or outcome.

relationTypes.name: reduces
relationTypes.def: Lowers a climate-risk dimension (exposure, vulnerability, sensitivity).

relationTypes.name: reduces-emissions
relationTypes.def: Mitigation: the subject reduces greenhouse-gas emissions of the object.

relationTypes.name: sequesters
relationTypes.def: Mitigation: the subject sequesters carbon in the object.

concepts.label: Climate
concepts.def: Average weather, or more rigorously, the statistical description in terms of the mean and variability of relevant quantities over a period of time ranging from months to thousands or millions of years.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGI Annex VII Glossary: Climate
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Climate impact
concepts.def: Consequence of realised climate-related risks on natural and human systems, referring to effects on lives, livelihoods, health and well-being, ecosystems and species, economic, social and cultural assets, services and infrastructure; impacts may be adverse or beneficial.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Climate risk
concepts.def: Potential for adverse consequences for human or ecological systems, arising from the dynamic interaction between climate-related hazards and the exposure and vulnerability of the affected systems.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic
concepts.example: CGIAR climate risk profiles assess exposure of agricultural value chains across crop, livestock, and fishery systems.

concepts.label: Compound climate risk
concepts.def: Climate risk that results from the combination of multiple climate hazards, drivers, or their interactions, whose joint occurrence produces consequences greater than those of the individual hazards alone.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGI Ch.11: Compound events
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Health risk
concepts.def: Potential for adverse health consequences - disease, injury, malnutrition or death - in human populations, treated as climate-related when attributable to climate hazards or climate-sensitive transmission pathways.
concepts.defSrc: WHO (environmental health risks); IPCC AR6 WGII Ch.7
concepts.aCond: Climate risk counts as adaptation when the text attributes it to climate change, climate variability, or a named climate hazard (for example climate-induced, climate-driven, exacerbated by warming, or due to changing rainfall), OR when it is the stated target of an adaptation-specific intervention, climate service, or early-warning action; NOT adaptation when it is described as a routine pest, sanitary, food-safety, land-management, or general social or economic problem with no climate framing.

concepts.label: Climate hazard
concepts.def: Potential occurrence of a climate-related physical event or trend that may cause loss of life, injury, or other health impacts, as well as damage and loss to property, infrastructure, livelihoods, service provision, ecosystems, and environmental resources.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Biological hazard
concepts.def: Climate hazard arising from living organisms whose distribution, abundance, or activity is influenced by climate variability or change, including pests, pathogens, and invasive species that harm agricultural and ecological systems.
concepts.aCond: Climate risk counts as adaptation when the text attributes it to climate change, climate variability, or a named climate hazard (for example climate-induced, climate-driven, exacerbated by warming, or due to changing rainfall), OR when it is the stated target of an adaptation-specific intervention, climate service, or early-warning action; NOT adaptation when it is described as a routine pest, sanitary, food-safety, land-management, or general social or economic problem with no climate framing.

concepts.label: Pest pressure
concepts.def: Biological hazard characterised by shifts in the distribution, abundance, or timing of pest or vector populations caused by climate variability or change, affecting crop, livestock, fishery, and livelihood systems.
concepts.aCond: Climate risk counts as adaptation when the text attributes it to climate change, climate variability, or a named climate hazard (for example climate-induced, climate-driven, exacerbated by warming, or due to changing rainfall), OR when it is the stated target of an adaptation-specific intervention, climate service, or early-warning action; NOT adaptation when it is described as a routine pest, sanitary, food-safety, land-management, or general social or economic problem with no climate framing.
concepts.example: CGIAR research addressed fall armyworm management and climate-linked pest risk in Africa.

concepts.label: Pest range expansion
concepts.def: Form of pest pressure characterised by the geographic spread of pests or vectors into areas that climate change has rendered newly suitable, exposing previously unaffected crops, livestock, and ecosystems.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGII Ch.2: Species range shifts
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Pest phenology disruption
concepts.def: Form of pest pressure characterised by climate-driven changes in the timing of pest or vector life-cycle events, such as emergence and reproduction, that alter their synchrony with hosts and crop calendars.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGII Ch.2: Phenology shifts; AGROVOC: phenology
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Disease pressure
concepts.def: Biological hazard characterised by shifts in the distribution, abundance, or timing of pathogen populations caused by climate variability or change, affecting crop, livestock, fishery, and livelihood systems.
concepts.aCond: Climate risk counts as adaptation when the text attributes it to climate change, climate variability, or a named climate hazard (for example climate-induced, climate-driven, exacerbated by warming, or due to changing rainfall), OR when it is the stated target of an adaptation-specific intervention, climate service, or early-warning action; NOT adaptation when it is described as a routine pest, sanitary, food-safety, land-management, or general social or economic problem with no climate framing.

concepts.label: Invasive species
concepts.def: Biological hazard characterised by the introduction and establishment of non-native species whose spread, facilitated by climate change, threatens crops, livestock, biodiversity, and ecosystem function.
concepts.aCond: Climate risk counts as adaptation when the text attributes it to climate change, climate variability, or a named climate hazard (for example climate-induced, climate-driven, exacerbated by warming, or due to changing rainfall), OR when it is the stated target of an adaptation-specific intervention, climate service, or early-warning action; NOT adaptation when it is described as a routine pest, sanitary, food-safety, land-management, or general social or economic problem with no climate framing.

concepts.label: Mycotoxin contamination
concepts.def: Biological hazard characterised by the accumulation of toxic secondary metabolites produced by fungi on crops, the incidence of which is influenced by climate-driven temperature and moisture conditions, threatening food and feed safety.
concepts.aCond: Climate risk counts as adaptation when the text attributes it to climate change, climate variability, or a named climate hazard (for example climate-induced, climate-driven, exacerbated by warming, or due to changing rainfall), OR when it is the stated target of an adaptation-specific intervention, climate service, or early-warning action; NOT adaptation when it is described as a routine pest, sanitary, food-safety, land-management, or general social or economic problem with no climate framing.

concepts.label: Zoonotic disease emergence
concepts.def: Biological hazard characterised by the emergence or spread of diseases transmissible between animals and humans, the dynamics of which are influenced by climate-driven changes in host, vector, and pathogen distributions.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGII Ch.7; WHO/FAO/WOAH One Health
concepts.aCond: Climate risk counts as adaptation when the text attributes it to climate change, climate variability, or a named climate hazard (for example climate-induced, climate-driven, exacerbated by warming, or due to changing rainfall), OR when it is the stated target of an adaptation-specific intervention, climate service, or early-warning action; NOT adaptation when it is described as a routine pest, sanitary, food-safety, land-management, or general social or economic problem with no climate framing.

concepts.label: Abiotic hazard
concepts.def: Climate hazard arising from non-living physical and chemical conditions of the atmosphere, water, land, and ocean, including temperature extremes, drought, flooding, storms, and soil degradation processes that harm agricultural and ecological systems.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Atmospheric hazard
concepts.def: Abiotic hazard originating in the atmosphere, comprising events and trends in temperature, precipitation, wind, and related weather phenomena that can harm agricultural and ecological systems.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Drought
concepts.def: Atmospheric hazard characterised by an exceptional period of water shortage for existing ecosystems and the human population, due to low precipitation, high temperature, and/or wind. Sub-types include meteorological, agricultural and ecological, and hydrological drought.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic
concepts.example: CIMMYT/IITA DTMA and STMA developed drought-tolerant maize varieties for farmers in drought-prone environments in sub-Saharan Africa.

concepts.label: Meteorological drought
concepts.def: Drought defined by a period with an abnormal precipitation deficit relative to the long-term average for a region.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGII Glossary: Drought (meteorological drought)
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Agricultural drought
concepts.def: Drought defined by an abnormal soil-moisture deficit, resulting from combined shortage of precipitation and excess evapotranspiration, that during the growing season impinges on crop production or ecosystem function.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGII Glossary: Drought (agricultural and ecological drought)
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Hydrological drought
concepts.def: Drought characterised by large runoff and water deficits in rivers, lakes and reservoirs.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGII Glossary: Drought (hydrological drought)
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Temperature extreme
concepts.def: Atmospheric hazard comprising air temperatures in the warm or cold tail of the local distribution, spanning both heat and cold extremes that exceed the tolerance thresholds of crops, livestock, people, and ecosystems.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Heat stress
concepts.def: Temperature extreme characterised by ambient thermal conditions, in particular elevated temperature and humidity, that exceed the tolerance thresholds of crops, livestock, or people and impair their performance, health, or survival.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Heatwave
concepts.def: Temperature extreme characterised by a period of abnormally hot weather, often defined relative to a temperature threshold, lasting from two days to months, with the potential to harm people, crops, livestock, and ecosystems.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Cold stress
concepts.def: Temperature extreme characterised by ambient temperatures low enough to impair the growth, development, health, or survival of crops, livestock, or people.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Frost
concepts.def: Cold stress characterised by the occurrence of air or surface temperatures at or below the freezing point of water, capable of damaging plant tissues and reducing crop yields.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Chilling stress
concepts.def: Cold stress characterised by low but non-freezing temperatures that impair the growth, development or yield of chilling-sensitive crops.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Wildfire
concepts.def: Atmospheric hazard characterised by an unplanned, uncontrolled fire burning in vegetation, the occurrence and severity of which are influenced by climate and weather, with the potential to destroy crops, forests, livestock, and infrastructure.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Fire-weather
concepts.def: Atmospheric hazard characterised by the meteorological conditions, including high temperature, low humidity, strong wind, and low precipitation, that promote the ignition and rapid spread of wildfire.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGI Ch.12: Fire weather
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Atmospheric chemistry change
concepts.def: Atmospheric hazard characterised by changes in the chemical composition of the atmosphere, such as elevated carbon dioxide concentration or surface ozone, that alter plant growth, productivity, and ecosystem function.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGI Ch.6; WGII Ch.5
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Storm
concepts.def: Atmospheric hazard characterised by a disturbance of the atmosphere marked by strong winds and often precipitation, thunder, or lightning, with the potential to damage crops, infrastructure, and livelihoods.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Tropical cyclone
concepts.def: Storm characterised by a strong, cyclonic-scale disturbance originating over tropical oceans; classed as a tropical storm at one-minute mean surface winds of 18 to 32 m/s, and as a hurricane, typhoon, or cyclone above 32 m/s depending on geographic location.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGI Annex VII Glossary: Tropical cyclone
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Hailstorm
concepts.def: Storm characterised by precipitation in the form of hail, in which balls or irregular lumps of ice fall from the atmosphere with sufficient force to damage crops, structures, and livestock.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Rainfall variability
concepts.def: Atmospheric hazard characterised by deviations in the timing, frequency, intensity, or spatial distribution of precipitation from expected long-term patterns, disrupting crop calendars and water availability.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGI Ch.8: Precipitation variability
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Erratic within-season rainfall
concepts.def: Form of rainfall variability characterised by unpredictable within-season timing, frequency, intensity, or spatial distribution of precipitation, which disrupts crop calendars and farm decisions; distinct from a lasting change in season timing and from sustained shortage or excess.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGI Ch.8: Precipitation variability
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic
concepts.example: PICSA integrates climate information with participatory decision tools to support farm planning under erratic rainfall across Africa and Latin America.

concepts.label: Shifted rainfall seasonality
concepts.def: Form of rainfall variability characterised by a lasting change in the onset, cessation, or duration of rainy seasons across years, making established crop calendars and livelihood practices less reliable; typically a slow-onset, climate-change-driven stressor distinct from within-season unpredictability.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGI Ch.8: Changes in monsoon and rainy-season timing
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic
concepts.example: CGIAR climate services in Rwanda used seasonal forecasts and historical climate information to support decision-making under shifting rainfall seasons.

concepts.label: Rainfall intensity change
concepts.def: Form of rainfall variability characterised by a change in the amount of precipitation falling per unit time, including increases in heavy and extreme precipitation that raise the risk of erosion, runoff, and flooding.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGI Ch.11: Extreme precipitation
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Dust storm
concepts.def: Storm characterised by strong winds lifting and transporting large quantities of dust or sand, which can damage crops, bury fields, reduce visibility, and degrade air quality and soils.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Hydrological hazard
concepts.def: Abiotic hazard relating to the occurrence, movement, and distribution of water at and below the land surface, comprising events such as floods and changes in water bodies that can harm agricultural and ecological systems.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGII Ch.3; IPCC SROCC
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Flood
concepts.def: Hydrological hazard characterised by the overflowing of the normal confines of a stream or other water body, or the accumulation of water over areas not normally submerged. Sub-types include fluvial, pluvial, flash, coastal, and glacial lake outburst floods.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic
concepts.example: IRRI Sub1 and next-generation flood-tolerant rice varieties target submergence and stagnant flooding in rice-growing communities.

concepts.label: Fluvial flood
concepts.def: Flood, also termed a river flood, characterised by the overflow of a watercourse onto adjacent floodplains when river discharge exceeds channel capacity.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGII Ch.4; AGROVOC: flooding (c_2980)
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Pluvial flood
concepts.def: Flood characterised by surface-water accumulation and waterlogging caused by rainfall exceeding the infiltration and drainage capacity of the land, independent of overflow from a watercourse.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGI Ch.11 (pluvial flooding); AGROVOC: waterlogging (c_8333)
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Coastal flood
concepts.def: Flood characterised by the inundation of low-lying coastal land by seawater, driven by storm surge, high tides, waves, or sea-level rise.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGII Ch.3; IPCC SROCC Ch.4
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Flash flood
concepts.def: Flood characterised by a rapid onset and short duration, generated by intense rainfall over a small or steep catchment, leaving little warning time and causing sudden, destructive inundation.
concepts.defSrc: AGROVOC: flash floods; IPCC AR6 WGI Ch.11
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Salinity intrusion
concepts.def: Hydrological hazard characterised by the inland or upward movement of saline water into freshwater aquifers, soils, or surface water, driven by sea-level rise, storm surge, or reduced freshwater flow, degrading water and soils for agriculture.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Glacier change
concepts.def: Hydrological hazard characterised by changes in the mass, extent, and behaviour of glaciers, including retreat and loss of ice, that alter the timing and volume of meltwater supply to downstream water resources.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Snowpack change
concepts.def: Hydrological hazard characterised by changes in the accumulation, extent, and melt timing of seasonal snow, altering the volume and seasonality of water supply from snowmelt to downstream systems.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Glacial lake outburst flood
concepts.def: Flood characterised by the sudden release of water impounded by a glacial lake, often following dam failure of moraine or ice, producing a destructive downstream flood.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC SROCC Ch.2: Glacial lake outburst flood
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Water scarcity
concepts.def: Hydrological hazard in which the demand for freshwater exceeds the available supply within a given geographic area and time period, intensifying as demand grows or as the quantity or quality of water resources declines.
concepts.defSrc: FAO / UN-Water (water scarcity); IPCC AR6 WGII Ch.4
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Soil hazard
concepts.def: Abiotic hazard relating to the soil and land system, comprising processes such as erosion, salinization, and degradation that are driven or accelerated by climate and that diminish the productive capacity of land.
concepts.aCond: Climate risk counts as adaptation when the text attributes it to climate change, climate variability, or a named climate hazard (for example climate-induced, climate-driven, exacerbated by warming, or due to changing rainfall), OR when it is the stated target of an adaptation-specific intervention, climate service, or early-warning action; NOT adaptation when it is described as a routine pest, sanitary, food-safety, land-management, or general social or economic problem with no climate framing.

concepts.label: Soil erosion
concepts.def: Soil hazard characterised by the detachment and removal of soil particles by water or wind, accelerated by extreme rainfall, runoff, and loss of vegetation cover, reducing soil depth and fertility.
concepts.aCond: Climate risk counts as adaptation when the text attributes it to climate change, climate variability, or a named climate hazard (for example climate-induced, climate-driven, exacerbated by warming, or due to changing rainfall), OR when it is the stated target of an adaptation-specific intervention, climate service, or early-warning action; NOT adaptation when it is described as a routine pest, sanitary, food-safety, land-management, or general social or economic problem with no climate framing.

concepts.label: Soil salinization
concepts.def: Soil hazard characterised by the accumulation of soluble salts in the soil profile, driven by factors such as evaporation, poor irrigation, and saline-water intrusion, which impairs plant growth and soil productivity.
concepts.aCond: Climate risk counts as adaptation when the text attributes it to climate change, climate variability, or a named climate hazard (for example climate-induced, climate-driven, exacerbated by warming, or due to changing rainfall), OR when it is the stated target of an adaptation-specific intervention, climate service, or early-warning action; NOT adaptation when it is described as a routine pest, sanitary, food-safety, land-management, or general social or economic problem with no climate framing.

concepts.label: Soil carbon loss
concepts.def: Soil hazard characterised by the depletion of soil organic carbon stocks through processes such as erosion, mineralization, and land-use change, reducing soil fertility, structure, and resilience to climate stress.
concepts.aCond: Climate risk counts as adaptation when the text attributes it to climate change, climate variability, or a named climate hazard (for example climate-induced, climate-driven, exacerbated by warming, or due to changing rainfall), OR when it is the stated target of an adaptation-specific intervention, climate service, or early-warning action; NOT adaptation when it is described as a routine pest, sanitary, food-safety, land-management, or general social or economic problem with no climate framing.

concepts.label: Soil acidification
concepts.def: Soil hazard characterised by a decline in soil pH, which mobilises toxic elements and reduces nutrient availability, impairing crop growth and soil health.
concepts.aCond: Climate risk counts as adaptation when the text attributes it to climate change, climate variability, or a named climate hazard (for example climate-induced, climate-driven, exacerbated by warming, or due to changing rainfall), OR when it is the stated target of an adaptation-specific intervention, climate service, or early-warning action; NOT adaptation when it is described as a routine pest, sanitary, food-safety, land-management, or general social or economic problem with no climate framing.

concepts.label: Desertification
concepts.def: Soil hazard characterised by land degradation in arid, semi-arid, and dry sub-humid areas resulting from climatic variations and human activities, reducing the biological and economic productivity of drylands.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Land degradation
concepts.def: Soil hazard characterised by a negative trend in land condition, caused by direct or indirect human-induced processes including anthropogenic climate change, expressed as a long-term reduction or loss of biological productivity, ecological integrity, or value to humans.
concepts.aCond: Climate risk counts as adaptation when the text attributes it to climate change, climate variability, or a named climate hazard (for example climate-induced, climate-driven, exacerbated by warming, or due to changing rainfall), OR when it is the stated target of an adaptation-specific intervention, climate service, or early-warning action; NOT adaptation when it is described as a routine pest, sanitary, food-safety, land-management, or general social or economic problem with no climate framing.
concepts.example: Climate-smart village work tested soil and water management and agroforestry options to address climate-driven soil degradation.

concepts.label: Marine hazard
concepts.def: Abiotic hazard originating in the ocean, comprising changes and events in sea level, temperature, chemistry, and circulation that can harm coastal, marine, and dependent agricultural and ecological systems.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Sea-level rise
concepts.def: Marine hazard characterised by the rise in the mean level of the ocean, driven by thermal expansion of seawater and loss of land ice, which exacerbates coastal flooding, erosion, and saltwater intrusion.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC SROCC Ch.4: Sea level rise
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Storm surge
concepts.def: Marine hazard characterised by the temporary rise in coastal water level above the predicted tide, driven by the winds and low atmospheric pressure of a storm, causing coastal flooding and damage.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC SROCC Ch.4; IPCC AR6 WGI Annex VII: Storm surge
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Marine heatwave
concepts.def: Marine hazard characterised by a period of abnormally high ocean temperature at a given location and time of year, lasting from days to months, with the potential to harm fisheries, aquaculture, and marine ecosystems.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Ocean warming
concepts.def: Marine hazard characterised by a gradual, sustained increase in ocean heat content and sea-surface temperature, altering marine productivity, species distributions, and fishery yields.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Ocean acidification
concepts.def: Marine hazard characterised by a reduction in the pH of ocean water caused by the uptake of atmospheric carbon dioxide, impairing calcifying organisms, fisheries, and aquaculture.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Ocean deoxygenation
concepts.def: Marine hazard characterised by a decline in the dissolved oxygen content of ocean waters, driven by warming and altered circulation, which stresses marine organisms and contracts viable fish habitat.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Compound hazard
concepts.def: Climate hazard arising from the combination of multiple drivers and/or hazards that contribute to societal or environmental risk, whether occurring simultaneously, in sequence, or compounding over time.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGI Ch.11: Compound events
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Cascading hazard
concepts.def: Climate hazard characterised by a chain of events in which an initial hazard triggers one or more secondary hazards or impacts, propagating across systems and sectors to amplify overall consequences.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGI Ch.11: Compound and cascading events
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Climate exposure
concepts.def: Climate risk component referring to the presence of people, livelihoods, species, ecosystems, infrastructure, or assets in places and settings that could be adversely affected by climate hazards.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Climate vulnerability
concepts.def: Climate risk component comprising the propensity of a system, community, or household to be adversely affected by climate variability and change, including sensitivity to harm and limited capacity to cope and adapt.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Climate sensitivity
concepts.def: Climate vulnerability component, comprising the degree to which a system, species, or activity is affected, beneficially or adversely, by a given change in climate conditions or by a climate hazard. Named in full to avoid collision with the physical-science term climate sensitivity, which denotes the warming response to a doubling of atmospheric carbon dioxide.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Tipping point
concepts.def: Critical threshold beyond which a system reorganises, often abruptly and/or irreversibly, in response to a relatively small additional change in conditions such as climate forcing.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGI Glossary: Tipping point
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Climate shock
concepts.def: Climate hazard with an acute temporal profile, marked by sudden, severe onset, such as a flood, storm, or rapid drought onset, that causes rapid harm, as distinct from a slow-onset stressor.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGII Glossary (Extreme weather event); resilience literature
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Climate stressor
concepts.def: Climate hazard with a chronic temporal profile, taking the form of a slow-onset or progressive pressure or trend, such as warming, shifting rainfall seasonality, or salinization, that gradually erodes a system, as distinct from an acute shock.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGII Glossary (Slow onset events); resilience literature
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Climate security
concepts.def: Dimension of climate risk describing the ways in which climate variability and change interact with social, economic, and political conditions to affect human security, including risks to livelihoods, to food and water access, to mobility, and to peace and stability.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Greenhouse gas
concepts.def: Gaseous constituent of the atmosphere, both natural and anthropogenic, that absorbs and re-emits infrared radiation and thereby contributes to warming of the lower atmosphere; the principal agricultural gases are carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide.
concepts.aCond: n/a (mitigation)

concepts.label: Carbon dioxide
concepts.def: Greenhouse gas released by respiration, combustion of carbon-bearing fuels, and land-use change, and the reference gas against which the warming effect of other gases is measured.
concepts.aCond: n/a (mitigation)

concepts.label: Methane
concepts.def: Greenhouse gas emitted by anaerobic processes such as enteric fermentation, flooded rice cultivation, and manure storage, with a high near-term warming effect.
concepts.aCond: n/a (mitigation)

concepts.label: Nitrous oxide
concepts.def: Greenhouse gas emitted mainly from soils following nitrogen inputs and from manure management, with a high global warming potential and long atmospheric lifetime.
concepts.aCond: n/a (mitigation)

concepts.label: Emission source
concepts.def: Process or activity that releases greenhouse gases to the atmosphere; in agri-food systems the principal sources include livestock digestion, flooded soils, nitrogen inputs, and land-use change.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC 2006 Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories
concepts.aCond: n/a (mitigation)

concepts.label: Enteric fermentation
concepts.def: Emission source consisting of the microbial digestion of feed in the digestive tract of ruminant livestock, which releases methane as a by-product.
concepts.aCond: n/a (mitigation)

concepts.label: Nitrogen fixation
concepts.def: Emission source consisting of the conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into reactive forms in soils and by leguminous plants, adding to the soil nitrogen available for nitrous oxide emission.
concepts.aCond: n/a (mitigation)

concepts.label: Climate change
concepts.def: Change in the state of the climate that can be identified by changes in the mean and/or variability of its properties and that persists for an extended period, typically decades or longer.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGI Glossary: Climate change
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Climate variability
concepts.def: Deviations of climate variables from a given mean state, including the occurrence of extremes, at all spatial and temporal scales beyond that of individual weather events.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGI Annex VII Glossary: Climate variability
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: El Nino-Southern Oscillation
concepts.def: Climate variability comprising the coupled ocean-atmosphere oscillation in the tropical Pacific that alternates between warm and cold phases on an interannual timescale.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGI Annex VII Glossary: El Nino-Southern Oscillation (ENSO)
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: El Nino
concepts.def: Warm phase of the El Nino-Southern Oscillation, in which weakened trade winds and warm sea-surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific shift rainfall and temperature patterns worldwide.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGI Annex VII Glossary: El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO)
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: La Nina
concepts.def: Cold phase of the El Nino-Southern Oscillation, in which strengthened trade winds and cool sea-surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific shift rainfall and temperature patterns worldwide.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGI Annex VII Glossary: El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO)
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Temperature
concepts.def: Climate variable measuring the degree of atmospheric or surface heat, whose averages, extremes and trends condition agricultural production and climate risk.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Humidity
concepts.def: Climate variable measuring the water-vapour content of the air, influencing heat stress, evapotranspiration, and pest and disease dynamics.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Soil moisture
concepts.def: Climate-related variable measuring the water held in soil, linking rainfall and temperature to crop water availability and drought development.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Dry season
concepts.def: Recurring period of the year with little or no rainfall, whose timing, length and intensity structure agricultural calendars and water availability.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Wet season
concepts.def: Recurring period of the year concentrating most annual rainfall, whose onset, length and intensity structure planting decisions and flood risk.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Rainfall
concepts.def: Climate variable measuring the depth of water reaching the ground as rain, whose totals, timing and intensity determine crop water availability.
concepts.defSrc: WMO/GCOS Essential Climate Variables (precipitation); AGROVOC: rainfall
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Coordination
concepts.def: Outcome construct denoting the degree of alignment and joint action among actors, sectors, or institutions involved in adaptation, treated neutrally as the result whose level may be strengthened or weakened.
concepts.defSrc: OECD (coordination of adaptation); IPCC AR6 WGII
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Social norms change
concepts.def: Outcome construct denoting a shift in the shared social rules, expectations, and practices that govern behaviour within a community, treated neutrally as the result whose direction in relation to adaptation is a separate facet.
concepts.defSrc: ALIGN (Advancing Learning and Innovation on Gender Norms)
concepts.srcSub: ALIGN (Advancing Learning and Innovation on Gender Norms)
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Knowledge
concepts.def: Outcome construct comprising the information and understanding that individuals, households, or institutions hold and can apply to adaptation.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGII (knowledge and capacity as enabling conditions for adaptation)
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Skills
concepts.def: Outcome construct comprising the practical competencies and know-how that individuals, households, or institutions can apply to adaptation.
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Agency
concepts.def: Outcome construct comprising the ability of individuals or groups to make and act on autonomous decisions about their lives and livelihoods in the context of adaptation.
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Capacity
concepts.def: Outcome construct denoting the abilities and assets that enable individuals, households, institutions, or systems to act on and adapt to climate change, treated neutrally as the result whose level may be built or eroded.
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Absorptive capacity
concepts.def: Capacity comprising the ability of people, institutions, organisations and systems, using available skills, values, beliefs, resources and opportunities, to address, manage and overcome adverse conditions in the short to medium term.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGII Glossary: Coping capacity (mapped to absorptive capacity)
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Adaptive capacity
concepts.def: Capacity comprising the ability of systems, institutions, humans and other organisms to adjust to potential damage, to take advantage of opportunities, or to respond to consequences.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGII Glossary: Adaptive capacity
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic
concepts.example: PICSA builds the capacity of farmers, pastoralists, and fisherfolk to combine forecasts, budgets, and options in adaptation decisions.

concepts.label: Transformative capacity
concepts.def: Capacity comprising the ability to create fundamentally new systems or to make fundamental changes when ecological, economic, or social structures render the existing system untenable in the face of climate change.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGII Glossary (Transformation); resilience literature
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Institutional capacity
concepts.def: Capacity comprising the ability of an organisation or institution to perform its functions effectively, efficiently, and sustainably, encompassing its human, financial, and adaptive-management resources.
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Resilience
concepts.def: Outcome construct denoting the capacity of interconnected social, economic and ecological systems to cope with a hazardous event, trend or disturbance, responding or reorganising in ways that maintain their essential function, identity and structure, while retaining the capacity for adaptation, learning and transformation.
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Climate resilience
concepts.def: Resilience specifically to climate-related hazards, comprising the capacity of a social, economic, or ecological system to anticipate, absorb, accommodate, or recover from the effects of a climate hazard while maintaining its essential function, identity, and structure.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Agricultural resilience
concepts.def: Resilience of agricultural production and livelihoods to shocks and stresses.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGII Glossary: Resilience (scoped to agriculture)
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Landscape resilience
concepts.def: Resilience of landscape-level ecological and social functions to shocks and stresses.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGII Glossary: Resilience (scoped to landscapes)
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Food system resilience
concepts.def: Resilience of food systems to shocks and stresses affecting production, supply chains and access.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGII Glossary: Resilience (scoped to food systems); HLPE
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Economic resilience
concepts.def: Resilience of incomes, assets and economic activity to shocks and stresses.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGII Glossary: Resilience (scoped to economies)
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Climate risk reduction
concepts.def: Outcome construct denoting a decrease in climate-related risk to a system, achieved by lowering hazard exposure, vulnerability, or sensitivity.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Wellbeing
concepts.def: Outcome construct denoting a state of existence that fulfils various human needs, including material living conditions and quality of life, as well as the ability to pursue one's goals, to thrive, and to feel satisfied with life.
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Adaptation effectiveness
concepts.def: Outcome construct denoting the extent to which an adaptation action is anticipated or observed to reduce climate-related risk.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Food loss
concepts.def: Outcome construct denoting the quantity or quality of food lost along the supply chain from production up to (but not including) the retail stage.
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Food waste
concepts.def: Outcome construct denoting the quantity or quality of food lost at the retail and consumption stages, including food discarded or left to spoil.
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Greenhouse gas emissions
concepts.def: Quantity of greenhouse gases released to the atmosphere by an activity, system, or territory over a defined period, expressed in carbon dioxide equivalent.
concepts.aCond: n/a (mitigation)

concepts.label: Carbon sequestered
concepts.def: Quantity of atmospheric carbon captured and stored in biomass, soils, or other reservoirs over a defined period.
concepts.aCond: n/a (mitigation)

concepts.label: Soil organic carbon
concepts.def: Quantity of carbon held in soil organic matter, a determinant of both soil health and terrestrial carbon storage.
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.
concepts.mCond: Outcome is measured by an emissions-referenced measure, OR is produced by a mitigation intervention; NOT mitigation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against emissions or removals.

concepts.label: Emission intensity
concepts.def: Greenhouse gas emissions per unit of agricultural output or activity.
concepts.aCond: n/a (mitigation)

concepts.label: Net zero emissions
concepts.def: Condition in which metric-weighted anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions are balanced by metric-weighted anthropogenic greenhouse gas removals over a defined period.
concepts.aCond: n/a (mitigation)

concepts.label: Energy efficiency
concepts.def: State in which a given service is delivered using less energy input, lowering fossil-fuel use and associated greenhouse gas emissions.
concepts.aCond: n/a (mitigation)

concepts.label: Nitrogen use efficiency
concepts.def: Ratio of nitrogen taken up in harvested product to nitrogen applied, a determinant of both agricultural productivity and nitrous oxide emissions.
concepts.aCond: n/a (mitigation)

concepts.label: Water use efficiency
concepts.def: Ratio of agricultural output to the volume of water used, a determinant of productivity and resilience under water scarcity.
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Equity
concepts.def: Outcome construct denoting the fair distribution of adaptation benefits, burdens, risks, and decision-making power across people and groups, accounting for differing needs, capacities, and historical disadvantage.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGII (equity and justice in adaptation)
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Social equity
concepts.def: Equity in the distribution of resources, opportunities and benefits across social groups.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGII (equity and justice in adaptation)
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Gender equity
concepts.def: Equity between women and men in the distribution of resources, opportunities and benefits.
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Inclusion
concepts.def: Outcome construct denoting the meaningful participation and benefit of all relevant groups, particularly those marginalised or differentially vulnerable, in adaptation decision-making and action.
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Gender inclusion
concepts.def: Inclusion of women and men on equitable terms in activities, institutions and benefits.
concepts.defSrc: CGIAR GENDER Impact Platform; IPCC AR6 WGII (inclusion)
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Social inclusion
concepts.def: Inclusion of marginalised or disadvantaged social groups in activities, institutions and benefits.
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Financial inclusion
concepts.def: Inclusion of individuals and enterprises in access to and use of affordable formal financial services.
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Youth inclusion
concepts.def: Inclusion of young people, addressing their distinct constraints, aspirations, and roles in agriculture and adaptation.
concepts.aCond: Cross-cutting concept applies to a qualifying intervention, outcome, or impact; NOT adaptation when applied generically with nothing qualifying to attach to.

concepts.label: Land Degradation Neutrality
concepts.def: Outcome construct denoting a state in which the amount and quality of land resources necessary to support ecosystem functions and food security remains stable or increases, by balancing land degradation against restoration and sustainable management.
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Loss and damage
concepts.def: Outcome construct denoting the adverse impacts of climate change that occur despite, or in the absence of, mitigation and adaptation, spanning both economic and non-economic harm.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Maladaptation
concepts.def: Outcome construct denoting a pattern in which actions intended as adaptation lead to increased or shifted climate risk, more inequitable outcomes, or diminished welfare, now or in the future.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Co-benefit
concepts.def: Outcome construct denoting a positive effect that an action taken for one climate objective has on another objective or on wider social and environmental goals.
concepts.aCond: Cross-cutting concept applies to a qualifying intervention, outcome, or impact; NOT adaptation when applied generically with nothing qualifying to attach to.
concepts.mCond: Cross-cutting concept applies to a mitigation intervention or outcome; NOT mitigation when applied generically.

concepts.label: Agronomic performance
concepts.def: Outcome construct denoting the field performance of crops or practices - establishment, growth and yield components.
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Behavioural change
concepts.def: Outcome construct denoting changes in the practices, decisions or habits of individuals or organisations.
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Employment
concepts.def: Outcome construct denoting paid work and jobs generated or sustained.
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Rate of return
concepts.def: Outcome construct denoting the financial or economic return generated per unit invested.
concepts.defSrc: CIMMYT (1988) From Agronomic Data to Farmer Recommendations; OECD
concepts.srcSub: CIMMYT (1988) From Agronomic Data to Farmer Recommendations
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Marginal rate of return
concepts.def: Rate of return on an additional unit of investment.
concepts.defSrc: CIMMYT (1988) From Agronomic Data to Farmer Recommendations (marginal rate of return)
concepts.srcSub: CIMMYT (1988) From Agronomic Data to Farmer Recommendations (marginal rate of return)
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Return on investment
concepts.def: Rate of return expressing net benefit as a share of investment cost.
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Food access
concepts.def: Outcome construct denoting the physical, social and economic access of people to sufficient, safe and nutritious food that meets their dietary needs.
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Loss avoided
concepts.def: Higher-order, long-term impact in which agricultural, economic, or welfare losses attributable to climate hazards are reduced as a result of an adaptation intervention, assessed against a credible counterfactual baseline without the intervention.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGII (avoided impacts / losses); UNFCCC WIM (loss and damage)
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic
concepts.example: Stress-tolerant maize, flood-tolerant rice, climate services, and IBLI generate evidence of climate-related losses avoided.

concepts.label: Agronomic loss avoided
concepts.def: Loss avoided in crop, livestock, fishery, aquaculture, or agroforestry production under climate stress, compared with a no-adaptation baseline, including avoided reductions in yield, productivity, production quality, or productive assets.
concepts.defSrc: IPCC AR6 WGII (avoided agricultural losses); FAO
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Welfare loss avoided
concepts.def: Loss avoided in household or community welfare under climate stress, compared with a no-adaptation baseline, including avoided reductions in income, food security, assets, labour capacity, or coping ability.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Avoided emissions
concepts.def: Higher-order mitigation effect consisting of greenhouse gas emissions prevented relative to a baseline or counterfactual.
concepts.aCond: n/a (mitigation)

concepts.label: Avoided land-use-change emissions
concepts.def: Avoided emissions consisting of the greenhouse gas release prevented by retaining existing land cover and its carbon stock rather than converting it to another use.
concepts.aCond: n/a (mitigation)

concepts.label: Availability
concepts.def: Stage of the adoption pathway at which an adaptation product, practice, service, or technology has been developed and exists in a form that could in principle reach intended users, prior to those users being able to obtain it.
concepts.aCond: Adoption pathway is a modifier, never standalone; counts as adaptation when the intervention, output, or outcome being made available, accessed, adopted, used, or scaled is itself adaptation-specific or hazard-addressing; NOT adaptation when the thing adopted or scaled is a generic (non-adaptation) technology, product, or practice.

concepts.label: Access
concepts.def: Stage of the adoption pathway at which intended users are able to reach and obtain an adaptation product, practice, service, or technology - in terms of physical, financial, and informational access - prior to actually taking it up.
concepts.aCond: Adoption pathway is a modifier, never standalone; counts as adaptation when the intervention, output, or outcome being made available, accessed, adopted, used, or scaled is itself adaptation-specific or hazard-addressing; NOT adaptation when the thing adopted or scaled is a generic (non-adaptation) technology, product, or practice.

concepts.label: Adoption
concepts.def: Stage of the adoption pathway at which an intended user takes up an adaptation product, practice, service, or technology for the first time, distinct from sustained use thereafter.
concepts.defSrc: AGROVOC (adoption of innovations); Rogers diffusion of innovations
concepts.aCond: Adoption pathway is a modifier, never standalone; counts as adaptation when the intervention, output, or outcome being made available, accessed, adopted, used, or scaled is itself adaptation-specific or hazard-addressing; NOT adaptation when the thing adopted or scaled is a generic (non-adaptation) technology, product, or practice.

concepts.label: Dis-adoption
concepts.def: Stage of the adoption pathway at which a user who had taken up an adaptation product, practice, service, or technology discontinues it, the reverse of adoption.
concepts.aCond: Adoption pathway is a modifier, never standalone; counts as adaptation when the intervention, output, or outcome being made available, accessed, adopted, used, or scaled is itself adaptation-specific or hazard-addressing; NOT adaptation when the thing adopted or scaled is a generic (non-adaptation) technology, product, or practice.

concepts.label: Use
concepts.def: Stage of the adoption pathway at which an adopter continues to apply an adaptation product, practice, service, or technology over time, reflecting sustained rather than one-off uptake.
concepts.aCond: Adoption pathway is a modifier, never standalone; counts as adaptation when the intervention, output, or outcome being made available, accessed, adopted, used, or scaled is itself adaptation-specific or hazard-addressing; NOT adaptation when the thing adopted or scaled is a generic (non-adaptation) technology, product, or practice.

concepts.label: Drought tolerance
concepts.def: Abiotic stress tolerance conferring the ability to maintain growth and yield under water-deficit (drought) conditions.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Heat tolerance
concepts.def: Abiotic stress tolerance conferring the ability to maintain growth and yield under high-temperature (heat) stress.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Submergence tolerance
concepts.def: Abiotic stress tolerance conferring the ability to survive temporary complete submergence or waterlogging during floods.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Salinity tolerance
concepts.def: Abiotic stress tolerance conferring the ability to maintain growth and yield under saline soil or water conditions.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Pest resistance
concepts.def: Heritable crop or breed trait conferring the ability to resist or limit damage from pests whose pressure shifts under climate change.
concepts.aCond: Breeding trait addresses a climate hazard, OR is part of a qualifying intervention, OR produces a hazard-conditioned outcome; NOT adaptation when selected purely for yield, quality, or market gain unrelated to a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Disease resistance
concepts.def: Heritable crop or breed trait conferring the ability to resist or limit damage from pathogens whose distribution shifts under climate change.
concepts.aCond: Breeding trait addresses a climate hazard, OR is part of a qualifying intervention, OR produces a hazard-conditioned outcome; NOT adaptation when selected purely for yield, quality, or market gain unrelated to a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Early maturity
concepts.def: Heritable crop trait by which a plant completes its growth cycle in a shorter period, allowing it to escape late-season drought or heat.
concepts.aCond: Breeding trait addresses a climate hazard, OR is part of a qualifying intervention, OR produces a hazard-conditioned outcome; NOT adaptation when selected purely for yield, quality, or market gain unrelated to a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Abiotic stress tolerance
concepts.def: Heritable crop trait conferring the ability to maintain growth and yield under non-living climate stresses such as drought, heat, flooding, or salinity.
concepts.aCond: Intrinsic

concepts.label: Low enteric methane
concepts.def: Heritable characteristic of ruminant livestock associated with lower enteric methane emission per unit of feed intake or product.
concepts.aCond: n/a (mitigation)

concepts.label: Producer
concepts.def: Actor category comprising individuals and households who cultivate crops, raise animals, or fish as a primary livelihood; includes smallholders, commercial producers, pastoralists, and fisherfolk.
concepts.defSrc: Actor category (CGIAR portfolio; no AGROVOC concept)
concepts.aCond: Stakeholder is engaged in a qualifying intervention (adopts, finances, or promotes), OR benefits from a qualifying outcome or impact; NOT adaptation when named only as an actor in a value chain or project, with no climate-risk role.
concepts.example: CGIAR breeding, climate service, and advisory programmes serve farmer communities across sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and Latin America. | Climate context: exposed to climate hazards.

concepts.label: Farmer
concepts.def: Producer who cultivates crops or raises livestock on a farm holding.
concepts.aCond: Stakeholder is engaged in a qualifying intervention (adopts, finances, or promotes), OR benefits from a qualifying outcome or impact; NOT adaptation when named only as an actor in a value chain or project, with no climate-risk role.

concepts.label: Smallholder farmer
concepts.def: Farmer who manages a small landholding, typically relying on family labour and facing high exposure to climate risk.
concepts.aCond: Stakeholder is engaged in a qualifying intervention (adopts, finances, or promotes), OR benefits from a qualifying outcome or impact; NOT adaptation when named only as an actor in a value chain or project, with no climate-risk role.
concepts.example: CIMMYT and IITA drought-tolerant maize programmes targeted smallholder farmers in drought-prone areas.

concepts.label: Commercial farmer
concepts.def: Farmer who manages a larger, market-oriented operation with greater capacity to invest in adaptation technologies.
concepts.aCond: Stakeholder is engaged in a qualifying intervention (adopts, finances, or promotes), OR benefits from a qualifying outcome or impact; NOT adaptation when named only as an actor in a value chain or project, with no climate-risk role.
concepts.example: CGIAR seed system and insurance work engages commercial farmers as delivery partners and adaptation technology adopters. | Climate context: exposed to climate-driven production and market risks.

concepts.label: Subsistence farmer
concepts.def: Farmer who grows crops or raises animals primarily for household consumption with minimal market surplus.
concepts.aCond: Stakeholder is engaged in a qualifying intervention (adopts, finances, or promotes), OR benefits from a qualifying outcome or impact; NOT adaptation when named only as an actor in a value chain or project, with no climate-risk role.
concepts.example: Climate context: vulnerable to climate-related production shocks.

concepts.label: Pastoralist
concepts.def: Producer whose primary livelihood depends on herding livestock in dryland or rangeland systems, with high exposure to climate-driven changes in rainfall, pasture, and water availability.
concepts.aCond: Stakeholder is engaged in a qualifying intervention (adopts, finances, or promotes), OR benefits from a qualifying outcome or impact; NOT adaptation when named only as an actor in a value chain or project, with no climate-risk role.
concepts.example: ILRI IBLI and pastoral livelihood programmes address climate risks for pastoral communities in the Horn of Africa.

concepts.label: Mobile pastoralist
concepts.def: Pastoralist who moves livestock seasonally across landscapes in response to rainfall and pasture availability, with high exposure to climate-driven rangeland degradation and limited access to services.
concepts.aCond: Stakeholder is engaged in a qualifying intervention (adopts, finances, or promotes), OR benefits from a qualifying outcome or impact; NOT adaptation when named only as an actor in a value chain or project, with no climate-risk role.
concepts.example: IBLI targets mobile pastoral households in northern Kenya and southern Ethiopia.

concepts.label: Agropastoralist
concepts.def: Pastoralist whose household combines crop farming with livestock keeping, using both as complementary risk-management strategies under climate stress.
concepts.aCond: Stakeholder is engaged in a qualifying intervention (adopts, finances, or promotes), OR benefits from a qualifying outcome or impact; NOT adaptation when named only as an actor in a value chain or project, with no climate-risk role.
concepts.example: CGIAR climate-smart village work addresses adaptation needs of agropastoral communities. | Climate context: exposed to climate risks affecting both production systems.

concepts.label: Fisherfolk
concepts.def: Producer whose primary livelihood depends on fishing or aquaculture, and who is affected by climate-driven changes in water temperature, water availability, fish stocks, and weather patterns.
concepts.aCond: Stakeholder is engaged in a qualifying intervention (adopts, finances, or promotes), OR benefits from a qualifying outcome or impact; NOT adaptation when named only as an actor in a value chain or project, with no climate-risk role.
concepts.example: WorldFish and CGIAR partners address climate risks for fishing and aquaculture communities.

concepts.label: Inland fisherfolk
concepts.def: Fisherfolk whose livelihood depends on freshwater fisheries in rivers, lakes, or reservoirs.
concepts.aCond: Stakeholder is engaged in a qualifying intervention (adopts, finances, or promotes), OR benefits from a qualifying outcome or impact; NOT adaptation when named only as an actor in a value chain or project, with no climate-risk role.

concepts.aCond: n/a (mitigation)

concepts.label: Scope 2 emissions
concepts.def: Indirect greenhouse gas emissions from the generation of purchased energy consumed by the reporting entity, as classified by the Greenhouse Gas Protocol.
concepts.aCond: n/a (mitigation)

concepts.label: Scope 3 emissions
concepts.def: Indirect greenhouse gas emissions, other than those in Scope 2, occurring in the reporting entity's value chain both upstream and downstream, as classified by the Greenhouse Gas Protocol.
concepts.aCond: n/a (mitigation)

concepts.label: Baseline scenario
concepts.def: Reference case describing the emissions that would occur without the mitigation activity or policy, against which reductions are measured.
concepts.aCond: n/a (mitigation)

concepts.label: Carbon sink
concepts.def: Reservoir or process, such as a forest, soil, or ocean, that removes and stores more carbon than it releases.
concepts.aCond: n/a (mitigation)

concepts.label: Water-energy-food nexus
concepts.def: Cross-cutting concept describing the interdependencies between water, energy, and food systems, used to analyse trade-offs and synergies when planning interventions that affect more than one of the three sectors.
concepts.aCond: Cross-cutting concept applies to a qualifying intervention, outcome, or impact; NOT adaptation when applied generically with nothing qualifying to attach to.
concepts.mCond: Cross-cutting concept applies to a mitigation intervention or outcome; NOT mitigation when applied generically.

concepts.label: Environmental damage
concepts.def: Cross-cutting concept denoting harm to ecosystems, natural resources or environmental quality.
concepts.aCond: Outcome is measured against a climate hazard (e.g. yield under drought), OR is produced by a qualifying intervention, OR an adaptation-specific principle or cross-cutting concept applies to it; NOT adaptation when it is a plain level or quantity result not framed against a climate stressor.

concepts.label: Resource recovery
concepts.def: Circular economy that recovers and reuses materials, nutrients, water or energy from waste streams.
concepts.defSrc: Ellen MacArthur Foundation (circular economy / resource recovery)
concepts.srcSub: Ellen MacArthur Foundation (circular economy / resource recovery)
concepts.aCond: Intervention addresses a climate hazard, OR produces a qualifying outcome (adaptation-specific or hazard-conditioned), OR produces an adaptation-specific impact; NOT adaptation when done purely for productivity, market, or development with no hazard link and no hazard-referenced result.

concepts.label: Peacebuilding
concepts.def: Cross-cutting concept denoting activities that reduce conflict drivers and strengthen the conditions for peace.
concepts.aCond: Intervention addresses a climate hazard, OR produces a qualifying outcome (adaptation-specific or hazard-conditioned), OR produces an adaptation-specific impact; NOT adaptation when done purely for productivity, market, or development with no hazard link and no hazard-referenced result.

concepts.label: Co-design
concepts.def: Cross-cutting concept denoting the joint development of interventions with their intended users and stakeholders.
concepts.aCond: Intervention addresses a climate hazard, OR produces a qualifying outcome (adaptation-specific or hazard-conditioned), OR produces an adaptation-specific impact; NOT adaptation when done purely for productivity, market, or development with no hazard link and no hazard-referenced result.

changes.label: Youth inclusion
changes.v4: Cross-cutting concept that intentionally engages young people and addresses their distinct constraints, aspirations, and roles in agriculture and adaptation.
changes.v5: Inclusion of young people, addressing their distinct constraints, aspirations, and roles in agriculture and adaptation.
