changes.label: Chilling stress
changes.v4: Cold stress characterised by physiological damage to plants exposed to low but non-freezing temperatures, impairing growth, development, and post-harvest quality, particularly in chilling-sensitive species.
changes.v5: Cold stress characterised by low but non-freezing temperatures that impair the growth, development or yield of chilling-sensitive crops.
changes.why: R10: reworded from the damage to the condition, to match the new label and its sibling Frost

changes.label: Dust storm
changes.v4: Atmospheric hazard characterised by strong winds lifting and transporting large quantities of dust or sand, which can damage crops, bury fields, reduce visibility, and degrade air quality and soils.
changes.v5: Storm characterised by strong winds lifting and transporting large quantities of dust or sand, which can damage crops, bury fields, reduce visibility, and degrade air quality and soils.
changes.why: changed by the 3 Sep cleanup; per-row reason in v5_hierarchy_decisions.md

changes.label: Sea-level rise
changes.v4: Oceanic hazard characterised by the rise in the mean level of the ocean, driven by thermal expansion of seawater and loss of land ice, which exacerbates coastal flooding, erosion, and saltwater intrusion.
changes.v5: Marine hazard characterised by the rise in the mean level of the ocean, driven by thermal expansion of seawater and loss of land ice, which exacerbates coastal flooding, erosion, and saltwater intrusion.
changes.why: R10: opener updated because the parent label changed from Oceanic hazard to Marine hazard

changes.label: Storm surge
changes.v4: Oceanic hazard characterised by the temporary rise in coastal water level above the predicted tide, driven by the winds and low atmospheric pressure of a storm, causing coastal flooding and damage.
changes.v5: Marine hazard characterised by the temporary rise in coastal water level above the predicted tide, driven by the winds and low atmospheric pressure of a storm, causing coastal flooding and damage.
changes.why: R10: opener updated because the parent label changed from Oceanic hazard to Marine hazard

changes.label: Glacial lake outburst flood
changes.v4: Hydrological hazard characterised by the sudden release of water impounded by a glacial lake, often following dam failure of moraine or ice, producing a destructive downstream flood.
changes.v5: Flood characterised by the sudden release of water impounded by a glacial lake, often following dam failure of moraine or ice, producing a destructive downstream flood.
changes.why: changed by the 3 Sep cleanup; per-row reason in v5_hierarchy_decisions.md

changes.label: Marine heatwave
changes.v4: Oceanic hazard characterised by a period of abnormally high ocean temperature at a given location and time of year, lasting from days to months, with the potential to harm fisheries, aquaculture, and marine ecosystems.
changes.v5: Marine hazard characterised by a period of abnormally high ocean temperature at a given location and time of year, lasting from days to months, with the potential to harm fisheries, aquaculture, and marine ecosystems.
changes.why: R10: opener updated because the parent label changed from Oceanic hazard to Marine hazard

changes.label: Ocean warming
changes.v4: Oceanic hazard characterised by a gradual, sustained increase in ocean heat content and sea-surface temperature, altering marine productivity, species distributions, and fishery yields.
changes.v5: Marine hazard characterised by a gradual, sustained increase in ocean heat content and sea-surface temperature, altering marine productivity, species distributions, and fishery yields.
changes.why: R10: opener updated because the parent label changed from Oceanic hazard to Marine hazard

changes.label: Ocean acidification
changes.v4: Oceanic hazard characterised by a reduction in the pH of ocean water caused by the uptake of atmospheric carbon dioxide, impairing calcifying organisms, fisheries, and aquaculture.
changes.v5: Marine hazard characterised by a reduction in the pH of ocean water caused by the uptake of atmospheric carbon dioxide, impairing calcifying organisms, fisheries, and aquaculture.
changes.why: R10: opener updated because the parent label changed from Oceanic hazard to Marine hazard

changes.label: Ocean deoxygenation
changes.v4: Oceanic hazard characterised by a decline in the dissolved oxygen content of ocean waters, driven by warming and altered circulation, which stresses marine organisms and contracts viable fish habitat.
changes.v5: Marine hazard characterised by a decline in the dissolved oxygen content of ocean waters, driven by warming and altered circulation, which stresses marine organisms and contracts viable fish habitat.
changes.why: R10: opener updated because the parent label changed from Oceanic hazard to Marine hazard

changes.label: Pest pressure
changes.v4: Biotic hazard characterised by shifts in the distribution, abundance, or timing of pest or vector populations caused by climate variability or change, affecting crop, livestock, fishery, and livelihood systems.
changes.v5: Biological hazard characterised by shifts in the distribution, abundance, or timing of pest or vector populations caused by climate variability or change, affecting crop, livestock, fishery, and livelihood systems.
changes.why: R10: opener updated because the parent label changed from Biotic hazard to Biological hazard

changes.label: Disease pressure
